speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been occurring and what do your stools look like?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ulcerative Colitis (Crohn's disease is less likely given the relief of pain with defecation and lack of fever/mass, but infectious colitis from campers cannot be fully ruled out without stool studies). The clinical picture of chronic bloody/mucoid diarrhea, urgency, and tenesmus strongly suggests inflammatory bowel disease. REQUEST TEST: Fecal Calprotectin, Stool O&P, and Stool Culture.
